spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Fail-CLOSED via startup-throw: each service throws InvalidOperationException at startup (builder-config phase, before app.Run()) when its auth key config is empty, mirroring the EXISTING fatal-config checks (ChatAnalysis Claude:ApiKey; WhatsAppAnalytics ConnectionStrings:PostgreSQL + Jwt:SecretKey). The request-path gates are then simplified so an empty key can never be treated as 'open'.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Previously an empty/unset auth key SILENTLY disabled the gate (ChatAnalysis /api/v1/analyze skipped the X-Internal-Api-Key check when internalApiKey was empty; WhatsAppAnalytics ValidateOpsKey returned true when Benchmark:OpsKey was empty, leaving ~25 /api/ops/* mutation endpoints open). A misconfigured production appsettings = unauthenticated endpoints. Q chose startup-throw (strongest) 2026-06-14.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: this is a deliberate fail-open -> fail-closed security hardening. The startup throw is the SAME pattern already used for Claude:ApiKey/pgConnStr/jwtSecretKey. OPERATIONAL DEPENDENCY (not a code bug): prod appsettings MUST set Benchmark:OpsKey + Microservice:InternalApiKey before deploy or the service will not boot — deploy is HELD (Q: commit'te dur), so the commit is safe and the keys are set before the eventual deploy.

plan.summary: Batch 3 of the 2026-06-14 refactor audit: close two fail-open auth defaults. (1) ChatAnalysis /api/v1/analyze only enforced X-Internal-Api-Key when Microservice:InternalApiKey was non-empty; now a startup throw guarantees the key, and the endpoint gate is unconditional. (2) WhatsAppAnalytics ValidateOpsKey returned true (open) when Benchmark:OpsKey was empty, exposing ~25 /api/ops/* endpoints; now a startup throw guarantees the key, and the open-mode branch is removed. Both throws mirror the services' existing fatal-config checks. No new error code (startup InvalidOperationException). Full-solution build PASS.
